note: What survives on film for the parishes of the Kvarner coast and the Vinodol, from the FamilySearch collection «Croatia, Church Books, 1516–1994» (cc 2040054). Almost none of it is name-indexed: these are images to be read page by page, and the point of listing them is to say exactly which volume to open.

parishes.name: Crikvenica
parishes.why: Births 1859–1896 holds all four children of Josip and Ana. Deaths 1893–1908 holds Marija Stjepanka, dead at twelve in 1905. And Marriages 1859–1908 is the single most valuable unopened volume in this archive: Josip and Ana married somewhere in the later 1880s, and if they married in his parish rather than hers, the entry is in this book.

parishes.name: Ledenice
parishes.why: Ana Kalanj's own baptism of 3 January 1864 is in Births 1861–1894 — the page the family already holds a scan of. Marriages 1866–1882 is the other candidate for her wedding, and marriages were commonly celebrated in the bride's parish. If they married in or after 1883 this parish's marriage film runs out and Crikvenica is the place to look.

parishes.name: Novi Vinodolski
parishes.why: The deepest run on this coast — baptisms from 1650. A Joannes Baptista De Franceski died at Crikvenica on 30 March 1801, a century before Josip came down from Istria, and if the name was already on the Vinodol then, these are the books that would show it.

parishes.name: Grižane
parishes.why: Note the Stanje duša of 1738 — a book of souls, the same kind of household register that broke this archive's Istrian line open.

parishes.name: Selce
parishes.why: The next parish along the coast from Crikvenica.

parishes.name: Senj
parishes.why: Where the line went next, in the generation after Ivan of 1925.

parishes.name: Fužine
parishes.why: Ruža Hreljac was born here on 13 February 1922. The volumes are not listed in the map extract; the browse link is live.

gap: Nothing on this film reaches 1936. The death of the Ana De Franceschi whose gravestone the family photographs — 28 May 1936 — falls outside every filmed volume, and would have to be asked for from the Croatian state archive at Rijeka or from the parish itself.
